description: Our strategy is to create outpost-building game on Mars/Moon environment.
summary: EXPERIMENTAL puts young learners in command of humanity’s first long-term experiment on the Moon: a four-person base at Shackleton Connecting Ridge, the lunar south pole site NASA chose for its Moon Base. Each day, players assign crew tasks, switch life-support systems on and off, and respond to emergencies like solar storms, micrometeorite hull breaches and moonquakes, while balancing power, oxygen, CO₂, water, food and radiation. Every number is grounded in NASA data, from the 0.84 kg of oxygen each astronaut breathes per day to the 250 mSv radiation limit and the solar-plus-reactor power plan. When the experiment fails, the game explains why, turning every mistake into a lesson about the trade-offs that decide whether a real mission succeeds.
details:
How it works
Every system is connected: life support needs power, solar panels go dark during shadow periods, oxygen is made from water, and every crew member can do only one job a day. When a mission fails, the end screen explains why.

Benefits
Students experience real engineering trade-offs through their own decisions instead of just reading about them, in a game that’s easy to learn and safe to fail.

Intended impact
To teach planning, prioritizing and problem-solving, and to spark interest in STEM and NASA’s return to the Moon.

Tools
Godot Engine 4.7 with GDScript, exported as a web build that runs in any browser, hosted on itch.io, with the source on GitHub under the MIT license. All the pixel art is original; the fonts are Kenney Fonts (CC0). An AI assistant helped with research and with drafting and debugging code.

Creativity
Players sit in a commander’s console inspired by real mission control. Screens come online as the base grows, events flash on an alert banner, and real lunar challenges, like multi-day construction, supply-lander delays and two-day shadow periods, become decisions players have to make.

Factors considered

  • Scientific accuracy: NASA figures, simplified only where needed for gameplay.
  • Young players: short text, icons, and colours paired with words.
  • Accessibility: browser play with nothing to install.
  • Replayability: random events and two mission lengths.
  • Scope: a design one developer could finish within the hackathon weekend.
